title: "Quesnel NRD connectivity"
subtitle: "Corrections and rerun, August 2026"
author: "Alex Chubaty"
date: last-modified
date-format: "[Last updated:] YYYY-MM-DD"
format:
  pdf:
    # Distinct from the Quesnel branch's `corrections-2026-08.pdf`. `Outputs/` is shared storage,
    # not per-branch, so without this the two versions of this report overwrite each other
    # depending on which was rendered last. Drop the suffix when the branches merge and there is
    # only one.
    output-file: corrections-2026-08-cariboo.pdf
    documentclass: article
    geometry: margin=2.5cm
    toc: true
    toc-depth: 2
    number-sections: true
    fig-pos: "H"
    pdf-engine: pdflatex
    urlcolor: blue
    include-in-header:
      text: |
        \usepackage{float}
        \floatplacement{figure}{H}
        %% Tables are floats too, and Quarto emits their `table` environment itself -- so
        %% kableExtra's `HOLD_position` has nothing left to pin. Pin them here instead, or a
        %% table drifts pages away from the paragraph that discusses it.
        \floatplacement{table}{H}
        %% kableExtra::linebreak() emits \makecell to wrap a column header onto two rows
        \usepackage{makecell}
        %% Keep a heading with the beginning of the text under it. LaTeX already refuses to break
        %% immediately after a heading, but nothing stops it breaking after the first line or two,
        %% which strands the heading at the foot of a page and reads as though the section were
        %% empty. \needspace reserves room for the heading plus a few lines and breaks the page
        %% first if it is not there.
        \usepackage{needspace}
        \let\oldsection\section
        \renewcommand{\section}{\needspace{5\baselineskip}\oldsection}
        \let\oldsubsection\subsection
        \renewcommand{\subsection}{\needspace{5\baselineskip}\oldsubsection}
        \let\oldsubsubsection\subsubsection
        \renewcommand{\subsubsection}{\needspace{5\baselineskip}\oldsubsubsection}
        %% and no single line of a paragraph left alone at the foot or head of a page
        \clubpenalty=10000
        \widowpenalty=10000

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = FALSE,
  message = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE,
  fig.align = "center",
  ## Keep figures in the section that discusses them. Captioned figures are LaTeX floats,
  ## so by default two full-width 4800 px maps drift to wherever they fit -- which put them
  ## pages away from the text about them. `H` (from the float package, loaded in the YAML
  ## header) pins them exactly where they appear in the source.
  fig.pos = "H",
  out.extra = ""
)

## knitr evaluates chunks in the directory of the input file, so anything that resolves the project
## by falling back to the working directory (`workflowtools::findProjectPath()` among them) reports
## `reports/` and every derived path silently misses. Walk up to the directory holding `_targets.R`.
find_project_root <- function(start = getwd()) {
  p <- normalizePath(start, mustWork = FALSE)
  while (!file.exists(file.path(p, "_targets.R")) && dirname(p) != p) {
    p <- dirname(p)
  }
  if (!file.exists(file.path(p, "_targets.R"))) {
    stop("could not locate the project root")
  }
  p
}

proj <- find_project_root()
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = proj)

## Emit native LaTeX tables rather than markdown ones. Pandoc turns a markdown table into a
## `longtable`, which splits across pages -- so a table lands half on one page and half on the next.
## `format = "latex"` with `booktabs` produces a `table` float instead, and floats never split; the
## preamble then pins them in place and sets them a size down.
options(knitr.table.format = "latex")

library(dplyr)
library(knitr)
library(targets)

## The pipeline is run once per Natural Resource District, and each district's inputs and results
## live under its own key. Quesnel is one district among them; nothing here is flat.
QUESNEL_OUT <- file.path(proj, "Outputs", "quesnel")

## Artefacts of the delivered (pre-correction) run, copied out of the way before the rerun
## overwrote them. See Appendix C, "Reproducing this report".
##
## The directory keeps the name it was given at the time; only the wording in this report changed.
DELIVERED <- file.path(proj, "Data", "processed", "quesnel", "published-2026-01-27")
## Derived from wherever `_targets` actually resolves to (it is usually a symlink to bulk storage),
## so no site-specific absolute path is baked into the repo. Override with the environment variable.
DELIVERED_META <- Sys.getenv(
  "BC_CONN_DELIVERED_META",
  file.path(
    dirname(normalizePath(file.path(proj, "_targets"), mustWork = FALSE)),
    "_targets_meta_backup_pre-2026-08-25-fixes"
  )
)
## Figures live beside this document, wherever it is. Building the path out of `proj` instead
## hardcodes the assumption that this file sits in `reports/`, and when project-root resolution
## slipped that assumption produced a nested `reports/reports/figures`.
rmd_dir <- tryCatch(dirname(knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE)), error = function(e) NULL)

if (is.null(rmd_dir) || !nzchar(rmd_dir) || is.na(rmd_dir)) {
  rmd_dir <- file.path(proj, "reports") ## sourcing the chunks outside knitr
}

FIGDIR <- normalizePath(file.path(rmd_dir, "figures"), mustWork = FALSE)
dir.create(FIGDIR, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

## Pandoc resolves an image path against the directory of the input file, and an ABSOLUTE path
## reaches LaTeX with a `.` glued to the front: `./home/achubaty/.../patches_delivered.png`, which
## does not exist and fails the build. rmarkdown did not do this, so the .Rmd could hand it the
## absolute path. Keep the absolute path for the existence check in R, which runs with the project
## root as its working directory, and give pandoc the relative one.
fig_rel <- function(f) file.path(basename(FIGDIR), basename(f))

## One place that decides how every table in this report is drawn.
##
## It draws the table body only. The caption, the number and the label come from the chunk's
## `#| tbl-cap` and `#| label: tbl-...` options, so that every table can be referred to as
## `@tbl-...` and no number in the prose can go stale. This also removes a whole class of defect:
## a caption written here was passed through to LaTeX unescaped, and a bare `%` in one silently
## centred every paragraph from that table to the end of the document. Captions handled by pandoc
## are escaped properly.
##
## `striped` shades alternate rows, which is what makes a table of more than a few rows readable
## across its full width.
##
## `widths` is a per-column width, e.g. c("8cm", "7cm"). A column given one wraps inside it;
## without one, a long cell sets the column to its own length and pushes the table off the page.
##
## Cell contents are plain text. `kbl()` escapes them, so they must not carry markdown: a backtick
## or a pair of asterisks would reach the page literally. Where a cell needs monospace or bold,
## build it with `kableExtra::cell_spec()` rather than marking it up by hand.
## `stripe_by` shades alternate *groups* of rows rather than alternate rows, for a table whose
## rows come in blocks: banding every second row across a block obscures the blocks, which are
## the thing the reader is trying to follow.
styled <- function(x, ..., widths = NULL, bold_rows = NULL, stripe_by = NULL) {
  latex_opts <- if (is.null(stripe_by)) "striped" else NULL

  ## `booktabs` inserts a gap after every fifth row by default, which lands wherever it lands: in
  ## a twelve-row table of four three-row blocks it fell inside the second and fourth blocks and
  ## read as though it meant something. Suppress it, and where the rows are grouped put the gap on
  ## the group boundaries instead, where it reinforces the shading rather than cutting across it.
  linesep <- ""
  if (!is.null(stripe_by)) {
    g <- match(stripe_by, unique(stripe_by))
    linesep <- ifelse(c(diff(g), 1) != 0, "\\addlinespace", "")
    linesep[length(linesep)] <- "" ## no gap between the last row and the bottom rule
  }

  k <- kableExtra::kbl(x, linesep = linesep, ...) |>
    kableExtra::kable_styling(latex_options = latex_opts, font_size = 9)

  if (!is.null(stripe_by)) {
    g <- match(stripe_by, unique(stripe_by))
    shaded <- which(g %% 2L == 0L)
    if (length(shaded)) {
      k <- kableExtra::row_spec(k, shaded, background = "#EFEFEF")
    }
  }

  for (i in seq_along(widths)) {
    if (nzchar(widths[i])) {
      k <- kableExtra::column_spec(k, i, width = widths[i])
    }
  }
  if (!is.null(bold_rows)) {
    k <- kableExtra::row_spec(k, bold_rows, bold = TRUE)
  }
  k
}

## Emit a table into a `results: asis` chunk.
##
## The surrounding blank lines are load-bearing: without them pandoc can read the table's LaTeX as
## a continuation of the preceding paragraph and start escaping parts of it into visible text while
## leaving others live.
emit <- function(k) cat("\n\n", as.character(k), "\n\n", sep = "")

ha <- function(x) sum(terra::expanse(x, unit = "ha", transform = FALSE))
num <- function(x, d = 1) formatC(round(x, d), format = "f", big.mark = ",", digits = d)

## Patch areas span five orders of magnitude within a single column, so a fixed number of decimal
## places is either unreadable at the top or meaningless at the bottom. Scientific notation keeps
## every row the same width and the same precision.
sci <- function(x, d = 2) formatC(x, format = "e", digits = d)
dur <- function(s) {
  ifelse(
    is.na(s),
    "n/a",
    ifelse(
      s >= 3600,
      sprintf("%.2f h", s / 3600),
      ifelse(s >= 60, sprintf("%.1f min", s / 60), sprintf("%.1f s", s))
    )
  )
}
have <- function(...) all(file.exists(...))

## `tar_read()` happily returns a target that has NOT been rebuilt: the store keeps the delivered
## run's object and metadata until the target is remade. Reading one of those and calling it
## "corrected" would silently compare the delivered run against itself. A target counts as rebuilt
## only where its recorded time differs from the delivered snapshot.
secs_by_name <- function(store) {
  if (!dir.exists(store)) {
    return(NULL)
  }
  m <- tar_meta(store = store, fields = c("name", "seconds"))
  stats::setNames(m$seconds, m$name)
}

PUB_SECONDS <- secs_by_name(DELIVERED_META)
CUR_SECONDS <- secs_by_name(file.path(proj, "_targets"))

is_rebuilt <- function(target) {
  if (is.null(PUB_SECONDS) || !target %in% names(PUB_SECONDS)) {
    return(TRUE)
  }
  if (is.null(CUR_SECONDS) || !target %in% names(CUR_SECONDS)) {
    return(FALSE)
  }
  cur <- CUR_SECONDS[[target]]
  if (is.na(cur)) {
    return(FALSE)
  }
  !isTRUE(all.equal(cur, unname(PUB_SECONDS[[target]])))
}
```

{{< pagebreak >}}

# Summary {#sec-summary}

An issue found in the seral-patch construction (commit `145cffb`) turned out to be one of several, and together they invalidate the connectivity results delivered in January 2026.
This report documents what was wrong, what the corrected numbers are, what the rerun cost, and why it needed to be rerun.

Omniscape reads two layers: the composite resistance surface and the composite source weights.
Both change materially.
Roughly half of what the delivered run treated as old interior forest was not forest at all, and a further large block of genuine old forest was modelled at the wrong resistance.
The Omniscape runs therefore had to be repeated rather than patched.

A second strand of work addressed the two largest spatial overlays.
Tiling the final resultant is done and took it from 5 h 52 min to 18 min.
Tiling the interior-forest overlay took it from 3 h 08 min to 6 min, reproducing the stored output exactly.
That matters here because the corrections below had to be applied, checked and re-applied several
times over, and a step measured in hours is one that cannot be retried casually.
It matters more for what comes next: the workflow is intended to cover the wider Cariboo, and
Cariboo-Chilcotin alone is roughly 2.4 times Quesnel's area, with these costs growing faster than
area rather than in step with it.
The retooling is a prerequisite for that extension rather than a refinement of it.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-summary-effects
#| tbl-cap: "Principal effects of the corrections."
data.frame(
  Item = c(
    "Seral layer, total area",
    "Old interior forest",
    "VRI x NDT-BEC layer, double-counted area",
    "Pipeline steps eliminated"
  ),
  Delivered = c("2,931,558 ha", "326,081.5 ha (13,783 polys)", "15,449.2 ha", "n/a"),
  Corrected = c("see Forest patches, below", "166,915.6 ha (10,348 polys)", "0.0 ha", "35.1 h of compute"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
) |>
  styled(booktabs = TRUE)
```

# Issues found and corrected {#sec-issues}

None of these produced an error.
Each produced numbers that looked reasonable, which is why they survived into the delivered results.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-issues
#| tbl-cap: "Issues corrected in this rerun, in the order the pipeline applies them. The numbering is referred to by the subsections that follow."
data.frame(
  `#` = seq_len(8),
  Issue = c(
    "The buffer that defines interior forest was removed from the mature-and-old class as well as from the old class",
    "Patches were not restricted to those actually classified as interior forest",
    "Interior forest overwrote the seral stage it was derived from",
    "Seral stages were assigned by spatial overlap rather than by splitting polygons at their boundaries",
    "The leading-species layer was combined with a tool that allows its outputs to overlap",
    "Slivers were removed by area rather than by the shared-edge rule the original scripts use",
    "Patch statistics were measured on overlay fragments rather than on whole patches",
    "Tile overlap for Omniscape was given in pixels where map units were expected"
  ),
  Consequence = c(
    "Mature-and-old interior forest came out identical to old-only interior forest",
    "50.8% of the area reported as old interior forest was unclassified land",
    "160,417 ha of old forest cores were modelled as ordinary forest instead of as the best available habitat",
    "The layer grew to 7.78 million polygons covering 39.5 million ha, far more than the study area holds",
    "22,628 ha of land was dropped and 15,449 ha was counted twice",
    "Slivers were merged into the wrong neighbouring polygon",
    "The smallest reported old patch was < 4.6e-6 m\u00b2",
    "Visible seams across the tiled test run"
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
  check.names = FALSE
) |>
  styled(
    booktabs = TRUE,
    row.names = FALSE,
    widths = c("0.6cm", "7.2cm", "7.2cm")
  )
```

The rest of this section gives the detail behind each, and the area figures that follow from them.
Issue 8 concerns how the Omniscape runs were tiled for benchmarking rather than the data itself, and is covered in [Appendix B](#sec-appendix-timings).

## Forest patches {#sec-forest-patches}

*Issues 1, 2, 3, 4 and 6.*

```{r patches-table}
pub_gpkg <- file.path(DELIVERED, "forest_patches_final.gpkg")
ok_patches <- have(pub_gpkg) &&
  !inherits(try(tar_read_raw("forest_patches_final"), silent = TRUE), "try-error") &&
  is_rebuilt("forest_patches_final")
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-patches-compare
#| tbl-cap: "Final resultant by seral stage. Resistance and source weight are assigned from the seral stage, so a stage that changes area moves that area between resistance classes."
#| eval: !expr ok_patches
tabulate_patches <- function(v) {
  v$ha <- terra::expanse(v, unit = "ha", transform = FALSE)
  as.data.frame(v) |>
    group_by(Seral, Resistance, SourceWt) |>
    summarise(n = n(), ha = sum(ha), .groups = "drop")
}

b <- terra::vect(pub_gpkg)
a <- tidyterra::as_spatvector(tar_read_raw("forest_patches_final"))

cmp <- full_join(
  tabulate_patches(b) |> rename(n_pub = n, ha_pub = ha),
  tabulate_patches(a) |> rename(n_cor = n, ha_cor = ha),
  by = c("Seral", "Resistance", "SourceWt")
) |>
  mutate(
    across(where(is.numeric), \(x) ifelse(is.na(x), 0, x)),
    d = ha_cor - ha_pub,
    pct = ifelse(ha_pub > 0, 100 * d / ha_pub, NA_real_)
  ) |>
  arrange(Resistance)

cmp |>
  transmute(
    Seral,
    Resistance,
    SourceWt,
    `Delivered (ha)` = num(ha_pub),
    `Corrected (ha)` = num(ha_cor),
    `Change (ha)` = num(d),
    `Change (%)` = num(pct)
  ) |>
  styled(
    booktabs = TRUE
  )
```

```{r patches-missing, eval = !ok_patches, results = "asis"}
cat("_The corrected `forest_patches_final` was not available when this was rendered._\n")
```

@fig-patches-delivered, @fig-patches-corrected and @fig-patches-change are drawn by the same code
from the same inputs, so any difference between them is a difference in the data rather than in how

```{r}
#| label: fig-patches-delivered
#| fig-cap: "Delivered patches, January 2026. Old forest is thin and fragmented; mature forest is near-continuous."
#| eval: !expr ok_patches
#| out-width: "100%"
targets::tar_source()
f <- file.path(FIGDIR, "patches_delivered.png")
## the writers return the path they wrote; at the top level of a chunk an `if` whose condition

if (!file.exists(f)) {

    b,

include_graphics(fig_rel(f), rel_path = FALSE, error = FALSE)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-patches-corrected
#| fig-cap: "Corrected patches, August 2026."
#| eval: !expr ok_patches
#| out-width: "100%"
f <- file.path(FIGDIR, "patches_corrected.png")
if (!file.exists(f)) {
```
